root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `object_delete_items()` calls `sdb_free(o->kv)`, the shared ART metadata `Sdb` must still have more than one live reference because the `info` namespace still aliases the same object through `ns->sdb`.
root_cause_criterion.description: In the vulnerable run, `destroy()` already consumed one reference from the shared ART metadata `Sdb`, so `object_delete_items()` reaches `sdb_free(o->kv)` with `o->kv->refs == 1` and frees the object while the `info` namespace still stores the raw pointer. In the fixed run, the destroy-side free is gone, so the same `object_delete_items()` call executes with `o->kv->refs == 2` and only decrements the still-live namespace-owned object to one reference.

nodes.state: `sdb_free(Sdb *s)` receives the stale `info`-namespace pointer as `s` and immediately evaluates `s->ht` and `s->refs`, which is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free read.
During recursive namespace teardown, the `info` namespace still retains the shared ART metadata pointer as `ns->sdb`.
`destroy()` calls `sdb_free(obj->kv)` on the shared ART metadata object before `object_delete_items()` later tears down `o->kv`.

edges.relation: The same ART metadata `Sdb *` finalized by `object_delete_items()` remains stored in the `info` namespace and is later reused as `ns->sdb` during namespace teardown.
The stale namespace pointer is passed unchanged from `ns_free()` into `sdb_free(Sdb *s)`, carrying the freed object directly to the sink.
The pointer prematurely released by `destroy()` is the same shared `Sdb *` later passed to `object_delete_items()` for the final free.
The `ao->kv` pointer stored under the `info` namespace in `load_buffer()` is the same pointer later loaded as `ns->sdb` during recursive namespace teardown.
